American Pachuco: The Legend of Luis Valdez Screening & Discussion • WXXI Studios

Events

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:03
Instaread

Join WXXI for a FREE screening of American Pachuco: The Legend of Luis Valdez, a film produced, written and directed by David Alvarado. Follow the legacy of filmmaker and playwright Luis Valdez. A founding figure of the Chicano Movement, Valdez is best known for his play Zoot Suit, the Ritchie Valens biopic La Bamba and the theatre company El Teatro Campesino.

The film screening will be followed by a panel discussion through 9pm.

Details:
“American Pachuco: The Legend of Luis Valdez” Screening & Panel Discussion
Thursday, October 1, 2026. Doors open at 6 p.m. Screening starts at 6:30 p.m. Panel ends at 9p.m.
WXXI Studio A
280 State Street, Rochester, NY 14614

Parking available next door at High Falls Garage.

This event is free, but reservations are required due to limited space. Event Details Here

The screening will run from 6:30-8:10pm, followed by a panel discussion which will end by 9pm

Reserve Your Spot


Panel Moderator: Julio Sáenz, WXXI Chief Content Officer.

Panelists:

Annette Ramos, Latinx Community Leader, Social Justice Advocate, Arts Curator & Executive Director Rochester Latino Theatre Company
Ricardo Figueroa, Director, School of Film and Animation at Rochester Institute of Technology & John Traver Endowed Professor 
Jason Barber, Co-Founder and Curator of ¡Presente! Film Series, Educator /Community Engagement Expert/Artist

Cover Photo: Luis Valdez in interview. Credit: Frasier Bradshaw.

About the film:
The son of migrant farmworkers who became a revolutionary artist, Luis Valdez changed American culture. In the 1960s, his El Teatro Campesino performed on flatbed trucks and helped mobilize farmworkers to win their first union contract. In 1979, his “Zoot Suit” was the first Chicano play ever performed on Broadway. His feature film, “La Bamba” was a breakout blockbuster in 1987 that authentically depicted Mexican American life and shared it with the world. Founded in 1965, Valdez’s El Teatro continues to be a beacon for Latino/a creators. American Pachuco is the story of a pioneering artist who gave voice to the overlooked and opened pathways for generations. Learn more at the American Masters’ Episode Website
